recentItems.description:
A severe cyclonic storm named Arnab has intensified in the west-central Bay of Bengal, prompting red alerts and cyclone warnings for coastal Andhra Pradesh and southern Odisha. The storm is currently centered approximately 170 km from Visakhapatnam, 140 km from Kakinada, 230 km from Machilipatnam, and 300 km from Bapatla. Over the past six hours, the cyclone has been moving at a speed of 18 km/h. The storm is expected to make landfall near Yanam, between Bapatla and Visakhapatnam, by tomorrow morning. At the time of landfall, wind speeds are forecast to reach 125–135 km/h, with gusts potentially peaking at up to 150 km/h.

Cyclone-related weather conditions are bringing rain and gusty winds across East Godavari and Konaseema districts of Andhra Pradesh. Rajamahendravaram and Kadiyam have experienced rain accompanied by strong winds. Heavy rainfall has also been reported across Konaseema, including Ambajipeta, Ravulapalem and Ainavilli mandals.
